A remembered NIP-44 decryption permission could reach more than messages.

Amber 6.6.5 now encrypts kind 30078 backups with a dedicated HKDF-derived key outside the NIP-44 derive-key namespace. Its release notes say this prevents an app with remembered nip44_decrypt access from reading backup payloads that can include per-app NIP-46 secrets and local keys.

The migration keeps a fallback for old backups until the next successful publish overwrites them. Amber 6.6.4 separately fixed a startup race that could contact relays over clearnet before the Tor setting loaded.

Two fixes, two boundaries: signer permission and transport choice. Neither release reports exploitation.

We checked the tagged releases, downloadable APKs and signed checksum manifests. Which version is actually installed matters more than which version exists upstream.
